_note: Pilot feature cards written by the LLM (role of 'make_cards'). 'confidence' = how sure the card author is about the text itself.

Amphiprion_ocellaris.card: Body oval, depth about half of standard length. Bright orange. Three white vertical bars: first just behind the eye curving forward behind the gill cover; second mid-body bulging forward toward the head as a wedge; third narrow on the caudal peduncle. Each white bar edged by a THIN black line (thin, not heavy). Fins orange with thin black margins. One continuous dorsal fin, 10-11 spines, spiny part tall and notched from soft part. Caudal fin rounded. Pelvic fins thoracic. No barbels.
Amphiprion_ocellaris.confuse: Amphiprion percula: percula has THICK black edging on bars and 10 dorsal spines; ocellaris edging is thin.

Oncorhynchus_mykiss.card: Fusiform salmonid body. One dorsal fin at mid-back PLUS a small fleshy ADIPOSE fin on the back near the tail. Pelvic fins abdominal, below the dorsal fin. Caudal fin shallowly forked to almost square. Back olive-green, sides silvery with a broad pink-red lateral band from gill cover to tail; pink-red gill cover. Many small black spots over back, upper sides, dorsal fin, adipose fin and the WHOLE caudal fin. Mouth terminal, jaw reaching just behind eye. No barbels.
Oncorhynchus_mykiss.confuse: Brown trout Salmo trutta has red and black spots with pale halos and few spots on tail; rainbow trout has only black spots, densely on tail, and a pink band.

Cyprinus_carpio.card: Robust, moderately deep body, back arched. Fully covered in large, regular scales. ONE long-based dorsal fin starting above pelvic fins, with a stout serrated spine at the front, running back to above the anal fin. Short anal fin with a serrated spine. TWO pairs of barbels: a short pair on the upper lip and a longer pair at the mouth corners. Mouth slightly inferior, protrusible. Caudal fin forked. Pelvic fins abdominal. Colour bronze-olive back, brassy-golden sides, yellowish belly; lower fins may be reddish-orange.
Cyprinus_carpio.confuse: Crucian carp Carassius has NO barbels; draw both barbel pairs.

Siniperca_chuatsi.card: Body deep and compressed, back strongly arched behind the head. Large mouth, lower jaw projecting beyond upper; maxilla reaches behind the eye. ONE continuous dorsal fin: about 12 strong spines then a rounded soft part. Anal fin with 3 spines. Caudal fin rounded. Pelvic fins thoracic. Scales very small. Colour yellowish-olive to golden-brown with irregular dark brown blotches and rosettes; a dark oblique stripe from the snout tip through the eye to the dorsal-fin origin; a large dark blotch mid-body below the spiny dorsal; soft fins with rows of dark spots.
Siniperca_chuatsi.confuse: Siniperca scherzeri has round ocellated spots, not irregular blotches; chuatsi has a much deeper body.

Larimichthys_crocea.card: Elongate, compressed body. Dorsal fin deeply notched: short spiny part almost separate from a long soft part. Caudal fin wedge-shaped / pointed. Anal fin with 2 spines, the second long. Caudal peduncle long and slender (length about 3x its depth). Pelvic fins thoracic. Lateral line runs to the caudal fin tip. Colour: back greyish golden-brown, lower sides and belly bright golden yellow; lips orange-red. Mouth terminal, oblique. No barbels.
Larimichthys_crocea.confuse: Small yellow croaker L. polyactis has a shorter, deeper caudal peduncle and larger scales.

Pterois_volitans.card: Body and head with alternating maroon-red and white vertical stripes, narrow stripes alternating with wider ones. Dorsal fin: 13 very long separated spines with partial membranes, banded red and white. Pectoral fins huge and fan-like with long, partly free banded rays. Soft dorsal, anal and caudal fins clear with rows of small dark spots. Fleshy tentacle above each eye. Pelvic fins thoracic. Caudal rounded.
Pterois_volitans.confuse: Pterois miles has fewer soft rays; not distinguishable visually - any classic red lionfish look is acceptable.

Chaetodon_auriga.card: Disc-shaped, highly compressed body; short pointed snout. Front two-thirds white with thin dark diagonal lines forming a right-angle chevron pattern (lines on front half slope up-backward, lines on rear half slope down-backward). Rear part of body, soft dorsal, anal and caudal fins yellow. Black vertical bar through the eye from nape to throat. Adult has a trailing filament from the soft dorsal fin and a black eyespot on the soft dorsal below the filament. Caudal fin truncate, yellow with a dark and pale submarginal band. One continuous dorsal fin. Pelvic fins thoracic.
Chaetodon_auriga.confuse: Chaetodon vagabundus has no filament and a black band on rear body and caudal.

Thalassoma_lunare.card: Elongate wrasse body. Body green with short vertical magenta/red lines on each scale giving a finely barred look. Head green with pink-red irregular bands radiating from the eye. Pectoral fin with a large magenta-pink and blue area. Caudal fin lunate with long pointed upper and lower lobes; centre of caudal yellow crescent, lobes pink-magenta. Dorsal and anal fins long, with a red stripe and blue edges. One long continuous dorsal fin. Pelvic fins thoracic, small.
Thalassoma_lunare.confuse: Thalassoma lutescens is yellow; T. lunare is green with a yellow moon-shaped caudal centre.

Betta_splendens.stage: adult male, WILD TYPE (short-finned, not aquarium long-fin variety)
Betta_splendens.card: Small elongate fish. Male: body dark reddish-brown with rows of iridescent blue-green scales. Fins red with blue-green iridescent streaks. Anal fin very long-based, from mid-belly to the caudal. Dorsal fin short and placed far back. Caudal fin rounded. Pelvic fins long, narrow, red with white tips. Mouth upturned. Fins moderately long, NOT the exaggerated veil-tail of aquarium varieties.
Betta_splendens.confuse: Aquarium betta varieties (veiltail, halfmoon) - do not draw these.

Silurus_asotus.card: Elongate catfish; head broad and flattened, body compressed toward the tail. Skin scaleless and slimy. NO adipose fin. Dorsal fin tiny (4-5 rays), set forward above the pectoral-pelvic gap. Anal fin extremely long, almost reaching the caudal fin (separated by a small notch). Caudal fin small, shallowly notched, upper lobe slightly longer. Adults have TWO pairs of barbels: one long pair at the upper jaw (reaching past pectoral fin) and one short pair on the chin. Small eyes. Wide mouth, lower jaw projecting. Colour mottled grey-olive to dark brown above, pale belly.
Silurus_asotus.confuse: Silurus meridionalis has a longer head; juvenile asotus has 3 barbel pairs - adults have 2.

Gadus_morhua.card: Heavy body. THREE separate dorsal fins and TWO separate anal fins, all soft-rayed and rounded. Prominent single chin barbel. Upper jaw overhangs lower. Pale lateral line curving upward over the pectoral fin. Pelvic fins jugular (on the throat, in front of the pectorals). Caudal fin square to slightly concave. Colour greenish-brown to reddish-brown with many small dark spots/freckles; belly pale.
Gadus_morhua.confuse: Haddock has a black lateral line and a dark shoulder blotch; cod has a pale lateral line.

Thunnus_albacares.card: Fusiform torpedo body. First dorsal spiny, yellowish. Second dorsal fin and anal fin long and sickle-shaped, bright yellow. 7-10 small yellow finlets edged black on top and bottom of the caudal peduncle behind the second dorsal and anal. Caudal fin lunate (crescent) with a lateral keel at its base. Pectoral fin long, reaching about to the second dorsal origin. Back dark metallic blue-black, a golden-yellow band along the side, belly silvery with broken vertical lines. Pelvic fins thoracic.
Thunnus_albacares.confuse: Bigeye tuna has shorter second dorsal/anal fins and no yellow band.

Carcharodon_carcharias.card: Stout spindle body, conical pointed snout. FIVE long gill slits in front of the pectoral fin. Large triangular first dorsal fin. Tiny second dorsal and tiny anal fin. Caudal fin crescent-shaped, nearly symmetrical, with a strong keel on the caudal peduncle. Large pectoral fins with dark tips underneath. Back slate grey with a sharp, irregular line to the white belly. Black eye. Mouth closed.
Carcharodon_carcharias.confuse: Shortfin mako is slimmer with a pointed snout and blue back; great white is heavier.

Sphyrna_lewini.view: lateral, body turned about 20 degrees toward viewer from above so the hammer outline is visible
Sphyrna_lewini.card: Head expanded into a broad hammer (cephalofoil); front edge arched with a central notch and scalloped indentations; eyes at the hammer tips. FIVE gill slits. Tall, falcate first dorsal. Low second dorsal with a long free rear tip. Caudal fin with a long upper lobe. Pectoral fins with dark tips underneath. Back grey-brown, belly white.
Sphyrna_lewini.confuse: Great hammerhead S. mokarran has a nearly straight front edge to the hammer and a very tall dorsal.

Paralichthys_olivaceus.view: eyed side, LEFT-eyed flatfish: both eyes on the left side; drawn eyed side up with the head pointing LEFT and dorsal fin along the top edge
Paralichthys_olivaceus.card: Oval, very compressed flatfish. BOTH eyes on the left (upper) side. Large mouth with strong teeth; maxilla reaching behind the lower eye. Dorsal fin starts above the eyes and runs to the caudal peduncle; anal fin long along the lower edge. Caudal fin rounded/double-truncate, separate. Eyed side olive-brown with scattered dark and whitish spots and a few larger dark spots. Pectoral fin visible on eyed side.
Paralichthys_olivaceus.confuse: Right-eyed flounders (Pleuronectidae) have eyes on the right side - must be LEFT-eyed here.

Hemitrygon_akajei.view: dorsal (top view), snout pointing LEFT, tail extending to the RIGHT
Hemitrygon_akajei.card: Top view of a rhomboid disc slightly wider than long; snout moderately angular. Eyes and spiracles on top of the head. Dorsal surface reddish-brown to brown, with yellowish-orange tint at the disc margin and in front of the eyes. A short row of small thorns along the mid-back. Whip-like tail about 1.5-2x disc length with a serrated venomous spine near its base, and a low skin fold on the tail. No dorsal fins on the tail before the spine.
Hemitrygon_akajei.confuse: Pastinachus/other stingrays lack the reddish tone; keep the reddish-brown dorsal colour.

Hippocampus_kuda.view: vertical, upright, head pointing LEFT, tail curled forward under the body
Hippocampus_kuda.card: Upright seahorse. Head at a right angle to the body, long tubular snout. Low rounded coronet. Body rings with low, rounded bumps (not spiny). Prehensile tail curled forward; NO caudal fin. Small transparent dorsal fin on the back; tiny pectoral fins behind the head; NO pelvic fins. Colour yellow to dark brown/black, often with small darker spots/granules.
Hippocampus_kuda.confuse: Hippocampus histrix has long spines; kuda is smooth.

Anguilla_japonica.view: lateral, whole length horizontal, slight S-curve allowed
Anguilla_japonica.card: Snake-like elongate body, round in front, compressed toward tail. Dorsal fin begins FAR behind the pectoral fin (about one third of body length from head), continuous with caudal and anal fins around the tail tip. NO pelvic fins. Small rounded pectoral fins. Lower jaw slightly longer than upper. Small gill slit just in front of pectoral. Skin smooth. Back dark olive to blackish, belly pale yellowish-white.
Anguilla_japonica.confuse: Moray eels have no pectoral fins; conger eels have dorsal fin starting near the pectoral.

Lophius_litulon.view: lateral (side view showing the fishing-rod lure)
Lophius_litulon.card: Huge broad flattened head, enormous wide mouth with lower jaw protruding and many sharp inward teeth; fringe of skin flaps around the jaw and head edges. First dorsal spine modified into a 'fishing rod' (illicium) on top of the snout with a fleshy lure at its tip; further free spines behind it, then a soft dorsal fin near the tail. Body tapers strongly behind the head. Pectoral fins arm-like. Pelvic fins small, on the throat. Caudal fin truncate. Colour yellowish-brown mottled with darker spots and pale ring-like marks.
Lophius_litulon.confuse: Lophius americanus is darker brown; litulon is yellowish.

Takifugu_rubripes.card: Elongate, rounded puffer body (not inflated). Beak-like fused teeth. A large black blotch with a white ring behind/above the pectoral fin. ANAL FIN WHITE. Small single dorsal fin set far back, opposite the anal. NO pelvic fins. Caudal fin truncate, dark. Back dark grey-black with indistinct small spots, belly white. Small spinules on back and belly.
Takifugu_rubripes.confuse: Takifugu chinensis has a BLACK anal fin; rubripes anal fin is WHITE.

Ostracion_cubicus.card: Body enclosed in a rigid box-like carapace of hexagonal plates; squarish in cross-section. Small single dorsal fin and anal fin set far back; NO pelvic fins. Caudal fin rounded on a short free peduncle. Small terminal mouth with fleshy pursed lips. Adult colour mustard-yellow to yellowish-brown with a small white or pale blue dot ringed black at the centre of each plate.
Ostracion_cubicus.confuse: Juveniles are bright yellow with black spots; draw the adult pattern of black-ringed pale dots.

Mola_mola.card: Disc-shaped body that looks cut off behind. NO true caudal fin: a rounded scalloped rim (clavus) with about 10-12 small rounded lobes joins the dorsal and anal fins. Tall dorsal and anal fins set far back, opposite each other. Small rounded pectoral fin. NO pelvic fins. Tiny beak-like mouth. Colour silvery grey to brownish with light mottling.
Mola_mola.confuse: Mola alexandrini has a rounded clavus with fewer ossicles and a bump on the head; keep mola's wavy clavus.

Latimeria_chalumnae.card: Heavy body with large scales. Fleshy LOBED fins on stalk-like bases: pectoral, pelvic, second dorsal and anal fins. First dorsal fan-like with spines. Diphycercal (three-lobed) tail: upper and lower lobes plus a small central lobe projecting from the middle. Colour deep steel-blue with irregular white blotches. Large head with big eye.
Latimeria_chalumnae.confuse: Latimeria menadoensis is brown; chalumnae is blue with white spots.

Lethenteron_camtschaticum.card: Eel-like jawless fish. Round oral sucking disc at the front (seen from the side). SEVEN round gill openings in a row behind the eye. NO paired fins (no pectoral, no pelvic). Two dorsal fins on the rear half, the second continuous with the caudal fin. Single nostril on top of the head. Colour grey-brown to bluish-grey above, paler below; second dorsal and caudal with dark tips.
Lethenteron_camtschaticum.confuse: Hagfish have barbels and no eyes visible; lampreys have 7 gill pores and a sucker.

Acipenser_sinensis.card: Long body with FIVE rows of bony scutes: one along the back, one along each side, one along each lower side. Long pointed conical snout. FOUR barbels in a row under the snout in front of the mouth. Mouth on the underside, transverse. Heterocercal tail with a long upper lobe. Single dorsal fin set far back. Pelvic fins abdominal. Back grey-blue to olive-brown, belly white.
Acipenser_sinensis.confuse: Dabry's sturgeon A. dabryanus has a shorter blunter snout.

Myxocyprinus_asiaticus.card: Adult: elongate body, back moderately humped. Long-based dorsal fin starting high at the front and running to the caudal peduncle (much less sail-like than in juveniles). Small inferior mouth with thick fleshy lips, NO barbels. Caudal fin forked. Pelvic fins abdominal. Adult colour pinkish-red to rouge with a broad crimson-red stripe along the mid-side from snout to tail; fins reddish.
Myxocyprinus_asiaticus.confuse: Juveniles have a tall sail-like dorsal and three dark oblique bars - do not draw the juvenile pattern.

Neocentropogon_japonicus.card: Small compressed scorpaenoid. Dorsal fin origin above or before the eye; long continuous dorsal with about 13-14 venomous spines with deeply notched membranes, then soft rays. Head with spines and ridges. Large pectoral fins. Pelvic fins thoracic. Caudal fin rounded. Live colour uncertain: pale pinkish-brown with darker irregular saddles and mottling.
Neocentropogon_japonicus.confuse: Other tetrarogid waspfishes; low confidence on colour.

Hemigobius_mingi.card: Small goby. TWO separate dorsal fins. Pelvic fins fused into a sucking disc. Caudal fin rounded to lanceolate. Body cylindrical in front, compressed behind. Colour yellowish-tan with several oblique dark brown bands slanting backward on the side.
Hemigobius_mingi.confuse: Hemigobius hoevenii has crescent-shaped bands; low confidence on exact pattern.

Pentapodus_berryae.card: Slender elongate nemipterid. One continuous dorsal fin (about 10 spines, 9 soft rays). Caudal fin forked. Pelvic fins thoracic. Large eye, small terminal mouth. Colour: back olive to greenish, a narrow yellow stripe and pale blue stripes along the side, belly whitish.
Pentapodus_berryae.confuse: Many Pentapodus species; low confidence on colour pattern.

Johnius_hypostoma.card: Croaker. Snout blunt, overhanging an inferior mouth; NO chin barbel. Dorsal fin deeply notched (spiny part almost separate). Caudal fin rhomboid / pointed. Second anal spine strong. Lateral line runs to the caudal tip. Colour silvery grey, darker on the back, fins dusky.
